notes.meaning: God challenges the people of Judah to show proof that He abandoned them or sold them off like an indebted father would sell his children. No such divorce paper or bill of sale exists. Their exile happened because of their own sins, not because the Lord was unfaithful or powerless.

The Lord asks why no one was waiting or listening when He spoke through His messengers. He asks if the people think His arm is too weak to rescue them from captivity. He reminds them of His ancient miracles at the Red Sea to prove He still has the power to save them.

God points to His supreme power over the skies, which He can cover in darkness just as someone puts on rough black sackcloth for mourning. This recalls the miraculous darkness sent upon Egypt and displays His authority over all creation. Nothing in heaven or on earth is beyond His control.

Here begins the third Servant Song, where God's promised Servant speaks. The Servant explains that God trained His tongue so He can bring timely comfort to those worn down by grief and affliction. Morning by morning the Father awakens Him so He can listen and learn like a faithful student.

The Servant explains that the Lord gave Him the willingness to hear and obey God's commands. Unlike the nation of Israel, which often turned away in stubbornness, the Servant never rebelled. He moved forward in complete obedience, even when the path meant deep personal suffering.

The Servant describes suffering severe physical beatings and public disgrace without fighting back. In the ancient world, tearing out someone's beard and spitting in their face were the ultimate signs of contempt. Christian readers see here an exact picture of Jesus willingly offering Himself to be mocked and beaten before His crucifixion.

Even amid cruel mistreatment, the Servant remains calm because He knows the Sovereign Lord will help Him. Setting His face like flint means having steady, rock-solid courage that refuses to back down. Because God is with Him, temporary insults cannot lead to lasting shame.

The Servant speaks like someone standing in a courtroom, confident that the Judge is on His side. To vindicate means to clear someone of false charges and show they did what is right. Because God will declare Him innocent, the Servant boldly challenges any human accuser to step forward.

The Servant repeats His strong faith that the Lord will stand by Him and clear His name. No human enemy has the power to pass a final guilty sentence on Him. All His accusers will eventually wear out and disappear, just like old clothes eaten away by moths.

A call goes out to those who revere the Lord and follow His Servant. Even sincere believers can walk through dark seasons of trial where they see very little comfort or light. In those hard times, they are urged to put their trust in God's faithful character and lean fully on Him.

differ.view: This verse speaks of an awakened sinner mourning over guilt and seeking the light of salvation, rather than a faithful believer living without assurance.
A sincere and obedient child of God can genuinely experience seasons where felt spiritual comfort and assurance are absent.

notes.meaning: A sharp warning is given to those who reject God's guidance and try to light their own path using human schemes and self-righteousness. Man-made torches and sparks offer only a brief glow that quickly dies out. Those who rely on their own devices instead of God will end up lying down in pain and sorrow.
